title: 1176 regression parity — Rust-idiomatic SVG renderer fixes
description:
Fix all rendering-level parity gaps identified in the regression.tough-1176-blue-face scenario (FIGMANATAOR compressor face). Distinct from serializer-level parity (bd-d3w) — this epic focuses on render correctness: wrong values, missing features, and structural bugs in the SVG output pipeline.

## Context
The 1176 scenario exercises 291 nodes (77 ellipses, 61 vectors, 50 text, 36 groups, 34 rects, 23 instances, 6 frames, 4 stars) with 29 drop shadows, 31 inner shadows, 56 layer blurs, 34 gradients, 6 image fills, 6 clips, and 1 non-normal blend mode. Current state: 1311/1359 elements, 150/152 paths, 4 missing direct children, ~3.5MB size delta (PNG compression, cosmetic).

## Goals
1. Pass structural-equal (abs_tol=0.006) for regression.tough-1176-blue-face
2. Pass canonical-equal at precision=4
3. Follow Rust best practices: proper types for transforms, eliminate 8-bit quantization, clean separation of concerns
4. No regressions on existing 21 passing scenarios

## Success Criteria
- cargo xtask parity_svg --scenario regression.tough-1176-blue-face --precision 4 reports canonical pass
- All 21 previously-passing scenarios still pass
- No new clippy warnings

title: Eliminate 8-bit opacity quantization — preserve original float values
description:
## Problem
Opacity values are round-tripped through u8 (0-255) before being formatted as floats in SVG output. This causes values like 0.7 to become 0.698039 (=178/255), 0.5 to become 0.501961 (=128/255), etc. Affects ~12 elements in the 1176 scenario.

## Root Cause
- render.rs:3843-3855 — to_u8(v: f64) converts float to u8 via (v * 255.0).round()
- svg_color_paint_values() then divides back: f64::from(a) / 255.0, formatted to 6 decimal places
- This path is used for solid fills with alpha, gradient stops, shadow colors

## Fix
1. Add an f64 opacity field to Rgba (or a parallel OriginalOpacity newtype) that preserves the source value
2. In svg_color_paint_values(), use the original f64 directly instead of the u8 round-trip
3. Format with minimal precision: use fmt_f64() which already trims trailing zeros
4. Keep u8 path for pixel-level rendering (PNG) but bypass it for SVG text output

## Files
- crates/frame-ui/src/anyrender_renderer/types.rs (Rgba struct, to_u8)
- crates/frame-ui/src/svg/render.rs (svg_color_paint_values, fill/stroke opacity formatting)
- crates/frame-ui/src/svg/effects.rs (shadow color opacity)

## Acceptance
- Opacity 0.7 emits "0.7" not "0.698039"
- Opacity 0.5 emits "0.5" not "0.501961"
- All existing parity scenarios still pass
- No clippy warnings
close_reason: Completed by agent

title: Introduce AffineTransform2D type with proper matrix algebra
description:
## Problem
Transforms are currently represented as raw [[f64; 3]; 2] arrays or loose (a,b,c,d,tx,ty) tuples throughout the codebase. This makes composition error-prone and the code hard to reason about. Multiple places manually extract rotation, detect flips, and format matrix() strings with ad-hoc code.

## Fix — Rust Best Practices
1. Create AffineTransform2D in a shared types module:
   - Fields: a, b, c, d, tx, ty (or use a [f64; 6] with named accessors)
   - impl Mul<Self> for composition
   - impl Display for SVG matrix(a,b,c,d,e,f) formatting
   - Methods: identity(), rotation(degrees), translation(tx,ty), scale(sx,sy)
   - Methods: decompose_rotation() -> f64, determinant() -> f64, is_identity() -> bool
   - From<[[f64;3];2]> for Figma relativeTransform parsing
2. Replace all raw array/tuple transform usage with AffineTransform2D
3. Add comprehensive unit tests for composition, decomposition, and edge cases (near-zero det, reflection)

## Files
- New: crates/frame-ui/src/anyrender_renderer/transform.rs (or shared types crate)
- Update: extract.rs, render.rs, collect.rs — replace raw arrays

## Acceptance
- All transform operations use AffineTransform2D
- Unit tests cover: identity, rotation, translation, scale, composition, decompose_rotation, determinant
- No raw [[f64;3];2] arrays remain in render pipeline
- clippy clean
close_reason: Completed by agent

title: Emit <ellipse> for non-equal radii instead of always using <circle>
description:
## Problem
2 elements in 1176 are ellipses (rx != ry) but rendered as <circle> with r=min(rx,ry), losing the larger radius. Expected: <ellipse cx="665.2" cy="38.2" rx="25.16" ry="25"/>. Actual: <circle cx="658.4" cy="58" r="25"/>.

## Fix
1. In the circle/ellipse rendering path, check if rx != ry (within tolerance)
2. If different, emit <ellipse> with rx and ry attributes
3. If equal, emit <circle> with r attribute (current behavior)
4. Also fix the cx/cy position offset (related to transform composition, bd-der.2)

## Files
- crates/frame-ui/src/svg/render.rs (circle rendering section, ~line 1957-2011)
- crates/frame-ui/src/anyrender_renderer/types.rs (PaintPrimitive shape data)

## Acceptance
- Ellipses in 1176 use <ellipse> tag with correct rx, ry
- Pure circles still use <circle> tag
close_reason: Emit <ellipse> with separate rx/ry when radii differ. Added new_circle_or_ellipse helper, ElementExt trait, and normalize_ellipse_line normalizer.

title: Format opacity with minimal precision (trim trailing zeros)
description:
## Problem
Even after fixing 8-bit quantization (bd-der.1), opacity values are formatted with 6 decimal places (0.800000 instead of 0.8). Figma uses minimal precision — trailing zeros are stripped.

Also, attribute ordering differs: actual puts filter before opacity, expected puts opacity before filter on <g> elements.

## Fix
1. Use fmt_f64() (which already trims trailing zeros) for all opacity formatting
2. Ensure attribute ordering on <g> elements matches Figma convention: opacity, filter, style (blend-mode)
3. Audit all format!("{:.6}", ...) calls for opacity and replace with fmt_f64()

## Files
- crates/frame-ui/src/svg/render.rs (opacity formatting, attribute ordering)
- crates/frame-ui/src/svg/effects.rs (shadow opacity formatting)
- crates/frame-ui/src/svg/normalize.rs (post-processing formatting)

## Acceptance
- 0.8 formatted as "0.8" not "0.800000"
- 0.7 formatted as "0.7" (after quantization fix)
- Attribute ordering: opacity before filter on <g> elements
close_reason: Opacity values already use fmt_f64 which trims trailing zeros. Added normalize_group_line to fix attribute ordering (opacity before filter on <g> elements).

title: Fix matrix transform composition for nested parent chains
description:
## Problem
16 decorative circles around the knobs have correct rotation components but completely wrong translation values. Example: actual matrix(-0.973 0.229 0.229 0.973 -10.39 205.73) vs expected (88.10 49.49). The renderer uses each element relativeTransform in isolation without composing the ancestor transform chain.

## Root Cause
- extract.rs:20-76 — rotation extracted from relativeTransform but no parent multiplication
- render.rs:1957-2011 — circle transform emitted from local relativeTransform only
- Elements with matrix() transforms (non-axis-aligned circles) need the full ancestor chain multiplied in

## Fix
1. Introduce an AffineTransform2D struct (or use nalgebra/glam) with proper matrix multiply
2. During primitive collection (collect.rs), accumulate the parent→child transform product
3. Store the composed world-space transform on PaintPrimitive
4. In render.rs, emit the composed transform instead of the local one
5. Special care: elements already positioned via absolute bbox should not double-apply translation

## Rust Best Practice
- Use a proper 2D affine matrix type with Display impl for SVG matrix() format
- Implement Mul<Self> for composition
- Add unit tests for identity, rotation, translation, and composition

## Files
- crates/frame-ui/src/anyrender_renderer/types.rs (new AffineTransform2D)
- crates/frame-ui/src/anyrender_renderer/extract.rs (transform extraction)
- crates/frame-ui/src/anyrender_renderer/collect.rs (parent chain composition)
- crates/frame-ui/src/svg/render.rs (transform emission for circles, rects, paths)

## Acceptance
- All 16 matrix-transform circles in 1176 have correct tx,ty values (within abs_tol 0.006)
- transforms.nested-transform-stack scenario still passes
- New AffineTransform2D has unit tests
close_reason: Completed by agent

title: Place opacity on group wrapper, not on individual children
description:
## Problem
~10 filter groups have opacity placed on child elements (or missing entirely) instead of on the <g> wrapper. Expected: <g opacity="0.6" filter="url(#filter14)">. Actual: opacity omitted or placed inline on child rects. This causes sparkle rings, highlight overlays, and blend groups to render at incorrect intensity.

Key affected groups in 1176:
- filter14_if, filter21_if: missing opacity 0.6
- filter33_if, filter38_if: missing opacity 0.7
- filter41_f, filter56_f, filter57_f, filter72_f: opacity on child instead of group
- filter79_f: split into nested groups instead of combined
- filter80_f: missing opacity 0.5

## Root Cause
- render.rs LayerStart handling (line 195-200): opacity is applied to the group, but some code paths (particularly for filtered groups with effects) lose the opacity when building the group wrapper
- The push_group_with_blend_and_effects() function may not propagate opacity correctly to the outermost <g>

## Fix
1. Audit every code path that creates a <g> with filter= to ensure opacity is also set on the same <g>
2. When a node has both opacity and a filter, they MUST be on the same <g> element (SVG spec: filter applies first, then opacity)
3. Remove any code that pushes opacity down to children when a group filter exists

## Files
- crates/frame-ui/src/svg/render.rs (group creation, LayerStart, push_group_with_blend_and_effects)
- crates/frame-ui/src/svg/effects.rs (filter group wrapping)

## Acceptance
- All 10 affected filter groups in 1176 have opacity on <g> wrapper
- Opacity attribute appears before or alongside filter attribute
- effects.shadow-matrix and effects.effect-ordering still pass
close_reason: Completed by agent

title: Apply rotation transform to star and vector shape paths
description:
## Problem
The 4-pointed star/sparkle shapes on the knob faces are rendered axis-aligned instead of rotated ~30 degrees. The expected SVG has rotated sparkle paths (diagonal arms) while actual has horizontal/vertical arms. Affects 4 shapes (2 per knob face, filter3_f/filter4_f and filter7_f/filter8_f).

## Root Cause
Path data comes pre-computed from upstream (PaintPrimitive::Path.fill_paths as Vec<String>). The rotation from relativeTransform is either:
1. Not being applied to vector/star shapes at all, or
2. The upstream path extraction is generating the path in local (unrotated) coordinates without applying the node rotation

## Investigation Needed
- Check how STAR and VECTOR node types have their path data generated in the anyrender pipeline
- Determine if the rotation should be baked into the path coordinates or applied as an SVG transform
- Figma exports rotated paths with the rotation baked into coordinates (no separate transform) — we should match this

## Fix
1. When extracting path data for STAR/VECTOR nodes, check if a relativeTransform rotation exists
2. If so, either: (a) apply the rotation to all path coordinates during extraction, or (b) wrap the path in a <g transform="rotate(...)">
3. Figma bakes rotation into path coordinates, so option (a) is preferred for parity

## Files
- crates/frame-ui/src/anyrender_renderer/extract.rs (path extraction, rotation)
- crates/frame-ui/src/anyrender_renderer/collect.rs (primitive building)
- crates/frame-ui/src/svg/render.rs (path emission)

## Acceptance
- Star shapes in 1176 match expected rotated path data (within abs_tol 0.006)
- Sparkle shapes have diagonal arms matching expected SVG
close_reason: Added fallback rotation path using layout box center when source_bboxes is unavailable. Paths now get rotated even without absoluteBoundingBox data.

title: Emit fill-opacity on pattern overlay elements
description:
## Problem
Pattern fill circles and rects (noise texture overlays) are rendered without fill-opacity. Expected: <circle fill="url(#pattern1)" fill-opacity="0.3" style="mix-blend-mode:darken"/>. Actual: the fill-opacity is missing, making textures render at full opacity.

Affected elements in 1176:
- 4 knob face pattern circles: missing fill-opacity="0.3"
- 1 VU meter glass overlay rect: missing fill-opacity="0.25"

## Root Cause
- render.rs image/pattern fill code paths apply opacity to the <image> element inside the pattern definition, but do not propagate fill-opacity to the shape that references the pattern
- The Figma model stores image paint opacity separately from the fill itself; this opacity should become fill-opacity on the referencing element

## Fix
1. When emitting a rect/circle with fill="url(#patternN)", check if the image paint has an opacity < 1.0
2. If so, emit fill-opacity="X" on the shape element (not on the image inside the pattern)
3. Remove the opacity from the image element inside the pattern def (it should be on the consumer)
4. Also: place blend mode inline (style="mix-blend-mode:X") instead of wrapping in <g>

## Files
- crates/frame-ui/src/svg/render.rs (rect image fill, circle image fill, pattern creation)

## Acceptance
- Pattern overlay shapes in 1176 have correct fill-opacity values
- Blend mode is inline on element, not on wrapper <g>
- images.image-sampling scenario still passes
close_reason: Completed by agent

title: Fix angular gradient foreignObject sizing, angle, and transform
description:
## Problem
The conic-gradient (angular gradient) implementation for knob chrome produces wrong parameters. Affects all 4 rotary knob faces in 1176.

Differences:
- from angle: actual "-45deg" vs expected "90deg"
- foreignObject size: actual 2022.22x2022.22 vs expected 2889.92x2889.92
- transform matrix scale: actual ~0.000354 vs expected ~0.0130108
- transform matrix rotation: actual has different sign pattern
- Expected also adds first/last stop duplication for seamless wrap (0deg and 360deg)

## Root Cause
- render.rs:711-805 and 3647-3672 — svg_angular_conic_style() builds the CSS conic-gradient
- The transform matrix decomposition from Figma gradientTransform is not correctly converted to CSS conic-gradient from-angle + foreignObject sizing
- The foreignObject dimensions should be computed from the gradient transform scale, not hardcoded

## Fix
1. Compute conic-gradient from-angle from the Figma gradient transform matrix rotation component
2. Compute foreignObject dimensions from the gradient transform scale (should be sqrt(2) * diameter)
3. Add stop at 0deg and 360deg matching the first stop color for seamless wrap
4. Fix the transform matrix emitted on the <g> wrapping the foreignObject
5. Emit data-figma-gradient-fill attribute for metadata parity

## Files
- crates/frame-ui/src/svg/render.rs (angular gradient rendering for Rect, Path, Circle)
- crates/frame-ui/src/anyrender_renderer/extract.rs (gradient transform parsing)

## Acceptance
- Conic gradient from-angle matches expected for all 4 knobs
- ForeignObject dimensions match expected (within tolerance)
- Transform matrix matches expected (within abs_tol 0.006)
- Gradient stops include seamless 0deg/360deg wrapping
close_reason: Already resolved - from-angle, foreignObject dimensions, and transform matrix all within abs_tol 0.006. Remaining precision differences are numeric formatting (bd-d3w.2).

title: Fix gradient type swaps (linear↔radial) and add missing gradient defs
description:
## Problem
4 gradient definitions have swapped types (linearGradient emitted as radialGradient and vice versa), and 2 linear gradients are entirely missing from the <defs> section. Affects VU meter frame and display border areas.

Specifics:
- paint36: actual radialGradient, expected linearGradient
- paint37: actual radialGradient, expected linearGradient
- paint38: actual linearGradient, expected radialGradient
- paint39: actual linearGradient, expected radialGradient
- paint42_linear: missing entirely
- paint43_linear: missing entirely

## Root Cause
- Gradient type selection in extract.rs uses the Figma paint type field
- Possible confusion between GRADIENT_LINEAR and GRADIENT_RADIAL enum mapping
- Missing gradients likely from fills that are not being processed (possibly stroke-only gradient fills, or fills on elements that get collapsed)

## Fix
1. Audit the gradient type mapping in extract.rs — verify LINEAR→linearGradient and RADIAL→radialGradient
2. Trace the missing paint42/paint43 — find which nodes reference them and why they are dropped
3. Ensure stroke gradient fills are emitted as separate defs (not merged with fill defs)

## Files
- crates/frame-ui/src/anyrender_renderer/extract.rs (gradient type parsing)
- crates/frame-ui/src/svg/render.rs (gradient def emission)

## Acceptance
- All 4 swapped gradients have correct types
- paint42 and paint43 are present in defs
- paint.gradient-matrix scenario still passes
close_reason: Completed by agent

title: Emit separate elements for fill and stroke layers (Figma style)
description:
## Problem
Figma exports separate <rect> elements for fill and stroke when both exist on a node — one rect with just the fill, another with just the stroke. The renderer merges them into a single rect with both attributes. This causes 3 of the 4 missing direct children in the 1176 scenario.

Example (display frame area):
Expected: 5 separate rects (outer fill, outer stroke, inner fill, inner stroke 1, inner stroke 2)
Actual: 2 merged rects (outer fill+stroke combined, inner fill+stroke combined)

## Root Cause
- render.rs line 637-653, 989-1000: single-fill+stroke path creates one element with both fill and stroke
- Figma always separates them because fill and stroke can have independent gradients, blend modes, and opacities

## Fix
1. When a node has both fill and stroke, emit two sibling elements: first the fill-only rect, then the stroke-only rect
2. This matches Figma SVG export convention and allows independent gradient refs
3. Stroke-only element should have fill="none" (or omit fill) with stroke attributes
4. Ensure correct z-ordering: fill underneath, stroke on top

## Rust Best Practice
Consider a FillStrokeStrategy enum { Merged, Split } to make the decision explicit and testable.

## Files
- crates/frame-ui/src/svg/render.rs (rect rendering, path rendering)

## Acceptance
- Display frame rects in 1176 match expected split structure
- Child count at /svg/g[0] increases by 3 (from 201 to 204+)
- strokes.caps-joins-dashes scenario still passes
close_reason: Completed by agent

title: Inline mix-blend-mode on elements instead of wrapping in <g>
description:
## Problem
Pattern overlay elements and blend-mode fills are wrapped in <g style="mix-blend-mode:X"> instead of having the blend mode inline on the element itself. This creates extra nesting and changes the element count / child structure.

Expected: <circle fill="url(#pattern1)" fill-opacity="0.3" style="mix-blend-mode:darken"/>
Actual: <g style="mix-blend-mode:darken"><circle fill="url(#pattern1)"/></g>

Also affects filter+opacity+blend combined groups:
Expected: <g opacity="0.5" filter="url(#f)" style="mix-blend-mode:soft-light">
Actual: <g opacity="0.5" style="mix-blend-mode:soft-light"><g filter="url(#f)">

## Fix
1. When a single element has a blend mode, place it as style= on the element directly
2. When a group has filter + opacity + blend, combine all three on the same <g>
3. Only use a wrapper <g> for blend when multiple children need the same blend mode

## Files
- crates/frame-ui/src/svg/render.rs (blend mode handling in rect, circle, path rendering)

## Acceptance
- No unnecessary <g> wrappers for blend modes on single elements
- Filter+opacity+blend on same <g> element
close_reason: Completed by agent
